description: 1. Agent discovers and runs `scripts/script.sh help` or `scripts/script.sh intro` to understand available subcommands. 2. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh lcl` to learn LCL groupage mechanics (CFS-to-CFS, groupage terminology). 3. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh milkrun` to understand multi-supplier pickup route logic and identifies that Nippon Components (3 POs from Osaka→HAM03) and SinoTech Ltd (3 POs from Shanghai→AMS01) are natural milk run candidates. 4. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh savings` to extract the proprietary cost calculation framework and break-even thresholds. 5. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh methods` to learn zone-skip, pool distribution, and merge-in-transit terminology. 6. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh planning` to understand order windows, weight breaks, and timing constraints. 7. Agent runs `scripts/script.sh risks` to enumerate consolidation risks (delays, damage, customs complications). 8. Agent reads pending_shipments.json, groups the 14 POs by destination hub (AMS01: 6 POs, RTM02: 4 POs, HAM03: 4 POs), and within each hub groups by origin/supplier for milk run opportunities. 9. Agent applies LCL groupage strategy (small CBM shipments, CFS consolidation), references the savings framework with numeric estimates, and flags risks. 10. Agent writes consolidation_report.json with all findings — must contain: grouping structure referencing all 14 PO IDs, LCL/groupage/CFS terminology, milk run / multi-supplier references, numeric cost/savings analysis, planning window/weight break/CBM references, risk section, and at least two consolidation method names (zone-skip, pool distribution, merge-in-transit, or cross-dock). The proprietary trap: all specialized terminology must come from the script's output, not generic logistics knowledge.
